Status values

Every status SATOM stores or shows — jobs, scheduled actions, change requests, processes, appliances and monitors, updates, HA roles, templates, certificates, Sentinel and more — with the exact value, its label and what it means.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
📍 WhereJob Manager, Scheduled Actions, Change Requests, Monitoring, Software Update, High Availability and other pages that show a status badge

Background jobs#

Shown in the Job Manager, the job dock and the job wait page. Stored in data/jobs/<id>.json.

Value Shown as Meaning
pending Pending Created, worker not started yet
running Running Working; progress and message update live. The wait page shows queued while a device job waits for another job's lock on the same appliance
pausing Pausing… Pause requested; the job stops at its next safe checkpoint
paused Paused Parked at a checkpoint until resumed
cancelling Stopping… Stop requested; finishing the current step
cancelled Stopped Stopped at a checkpoint (any registered compensations were run)
success Success Finished
error Error Failed; the message gives the reason

Active states are pending, running, cancelling, pausing, paused; terminal states are success, error, cancelled. Stop and pause are cooperative: an in-flight write to an appliance is never interrupted.

ℹ️Note — Orphaned jobs

When the service restarts, the worker threads die. At start-up and at most every two minutes afterwards, SATOM marks active jobs whose process no longer exists (or that never started within 10 minutes) as error with the message "Orphaned — the service restarted while this job was running."

See Jobs.

Scheduled actions#

Run status#

Each execution is a run row; the action's Last status column shows the latest one.

Value Badge Meaning
running running Run in progress. On the Scheduled Actions table the badge is driven by the action's run lease, so it shows exactly while the action is running
ok ok Every target succeeded
failed failed At least one target failed, the action is unknown, or the run crashed. A run left open by a dead process is closed as failed
skipped skipped Nothing ran: all targets in maintenance, no matching appliance, or the action needs an approved change request inside its window
missed missed (yellow) The scheduler was not running at the due time (or found the action overdue) with catch-up off and moved it to its next run without running it

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: missed has its own badge (it used to appear as "—"), the running badge now shows while an action is actually running, and a change request can only be approved from draft and cannot be cancelled once it is completed, failed or cancelled.

Run trigger#

schedule (fired by the scheduler), api (REST API v1) or manual (run from the page or the CLI). See Scheduled actions.

Schedule kinds#

once, interval, daily, weekly, monthly.

Change requests#

Value Badge colour Meaning
draft grey Being written, or approval voided by an edit
approved blue (info) Approved; can be scheduled
scheduled blue Bound to a scheduled action inside its window
in_progress blue The bound action has started
completed green The bound action finished ok
failed red The bound action finished with any other outcome — including skipped
cancelled grey Cancelled; its bound action was disabled

Terminal: completed, failed, cancelled.

From To When
draft approved Approve (users.manage); refused from any other status
approved, scheduled scheduled Schedule — needs a window start and a change type with an executor
approved, scheduled draft An edit voids the approval; the bound action is disabled and re-approval is required
approved, scheduled, in_progress in_progress The bound action fires inside the window
any non-terminal completed / failed The run finishes
any non-terminal (including in_progress) cancelled Cancel; refused once the change request is completed, failed or cancelled, so the recorded outcome is kept

A bound action may only run while the change request is approved, scheduled or in_progress and the clock is inside the window.

Related values on a change request: risk low / medium / high; notify status none / drafted / sent; external maintenance-window state none / open / closed / error. See Change requests.

Processes#

Kind Values
Run status running, waiting (parked on a manual gate — a person must answer), done, aborted
Verdict (when done) ok (every step ran and passed), partial (nothing failed, but something could not be checked), failed (a step failed)
Step outcome pass, fail, unknown (the system could not look — never counted as a failure), skipped (downstream of a stopped path — never counted as a pass)
Edge branch always, pass, fail, unknown

See Process.

Appliances and monitoring#

Appliance reachability#

Value Meaning
online The last status probe reached the appliance
offline The probe failed
unknown Never checked (default), or the appliance was removed during the check

The status is re-probed when the list is loaded and the stored value is older than 20 seconds.

Device health#

Monitoring rolls four signals — Harvest (sync runs), Cache (age of the newest snapshot), Deep monitors and Capacity — into one status:

Value Meaning
ok At least one measured-good signal and nothing worse
warn One sync error, cache older than the stale limit (default 6 h), a probe warning or a probe that could not run
crit 3 consecutive sync errors, cache older than 4 × the stale limit, or a critical probe
unknown Nothing measured (for example, never synced) — never shown as healthy

See Device health.

Deep monitors and probes#

Value Meaning
ok Within thresholds
warn Above the warning threshold
crit Above the critical threshold
error The probe could not run (SSH refused, timeout)
unknown Not run yet (default)

A suppressed probe keeps running and showing its status but no longer raises the device roll-up or mail until the suppression expires. See Deep monitors.

Rediscovery#

running, deep-running (deep capture), cli-running (CLI capture), done. See Rediscovery.

Appliance HA (FortiWeb / FortiADC clusters)#

Roles read from an appliance: primary, secondary, standalone, unknown. SATOM only reports primary when the appliance states it explicitly. HA inventory: clustered, standalone, unknown.

SATOM node, updates and HA#

Kind Values
Node role primary (database read-write), standby (streaming replica), unknown
HA mode ha or standalone
Reconciler deploy mode manual (observe only — default) or auto (drive the staged update)
Update / privileged request queued → running → success or failed (with rolled_back true/false)
Health probe /healthz/primary 200 {"role": "primary"}, 503 {"role": "standby"} or {"role": "unknown"}

See Software update and High availability.

Templates, plugins and scripts#

Object Values
Configuration template approval pending, approved (fleet-deployable), rejected — approving needs operations.template_approve
Plugin draft, testing (previewable by the author), published (in the navigation)
Lua script draft, tested, deployed
Scout (AI assistant) proposal pending, applied, dismissed

Certificates#

Managed certificates: pending (deployed, not bound yet), active, expiring (inside the renew-before window), superseded, revoked. See Certificates.

Integrations#

Integration hook runs: queued, running, ok, failed, timeout. See Integrations.

API library#

Kind Values
Build status measured, vendor_only, unmeasured, unknown_firmware
Endpoint on a build measured, blind, unmeasured, absent

See API library.

Sentinel#

Object Values
Incident open, verifying, mitigated, closed, false_positive
Response action proposed, approved, queued, applied, failed, expired, rolled_back, rejected

See Sentinel.

Notifications and alerts#

Object Values
Notification (bell) info, success, warning, error
Alert routing severity info, warning, critical
Bug report open, resolved

Edit locks#

An editor holds a lease on a resource (for example one server policy on one appliance). The browser renews it every 30 seconds; without renewal it expires after 120 seconds and another user can take over. See Locks.

#status#state#badge#lifecycle#pending#running#success#error#failed#skipped#missed#draft#approved#scheduled#in_progress#completed#cancelled#online#offline#unknown#primary#standby
